trickyParts: Rule 6 is the two-clause hazard rule of the plan, not the spec's literal 'reads needs.<job>.outputs' trigger: the literal rule would flag the three correct *_build conditions and miss the result-only shape; the plan records this as spec departures 1 and 2 (six conditions change, not three).

6b counts any upstream job with an if: key as skippable, including one on always(); a job with no if: of its own is never checked, which is why the fixture's worker_image (needs a job with an if:, has none itself) stays green.

The string-literal strip keeps a quoted index key (needs['x']) so the index form stays readable after the strip; a YAML plain scalar cannot start with a quote, so the quoted-always() case uses a double-quoted YAML scalar.

The ce-simplify-code pass applied three findings on the checker (needs_of moved beside the other generic job readers, 6a collects the tested results once instead of rescanning per read, ancestors' name annotated) → head bfacb40e; A1/A2 and both negative controls were re-run there with identical output.
